newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds off a notch, but seen supported.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds off a notch, but seen supported.

text.p: *Australain bonds a notch softer in thin trade at the open, with the market seen supported as it waits on Thursday's labour force data for July.

Australian bonds opened slightly weaker across the curve after Treasuries eased on the first day of U.S. quarterly refunding auctions, but the market was seen well supported ahead of Thursday's labour force data.
The U.S. auctioned $16 billion of three year notes on Tuesday, and will sell a further $22 billion of 10-year notes and 30-year bonds over the next two days.

That extra supply, combined with some emerging concerns after recent strong data that U.S. rates could rise in August or September, saw Treasuries end the day softer, and local bonds nudged lower as there was little else to guide them.
The market's focus is Thursday's July labour force data, which is expected to show the jobs market remains stalled, a situation that would be supportive of bonds.
Economists' forecasts centre on a 25,000 rise in employment, and for the unemployment rate to edge up to 8.6 percent.
With employment showing few signs of life, inflation low and growth still sluggish, bonds are expected to remain supported in the face of any further U.S. bearishness, traders said.
Westpac technical analyst Peter Pontikas said the 10-year bond future needed to close below 93.40 to upset the view that the Friday night's U.S. led sell off was only a dip to buy into.

Short end extends Tuesday's spread narrowing, while long end flat to narrower. NZ yields weighed on by profit-taking after eurobond issue. With slight weakness fairly even across maturities, yield curve remains steady.
